title: True Lilies Are Poisonous to Cats, Even the Vase Water 💐 (Things Living In Your House #71)
description:
Are lilies poisonous to cats? True lilies and daylilies are: the FDA says the entire lily plant is toxic to cats, the stem, leaves, flowers, pollen and even the water in a vase. Eating a small amount of a leaf or petal, licking a few pollen grains off its fur, or drinking the vase water can cause a cat to develop fatal kidney failure in less than 3 days. If treatment is delayed by 18 hours or more, the kidney failure is generally irreversible, so if you think your cat ate any part of a lily, licked its pollen or drank the vase water, call your veterinarian or a pet poison control center right away. The kinds the FDA names include Easter, Stargazer, Tiger and Asiatic lilies, plus daylilies. Plants like peace lilies and calla lilies are not true lilies and are a different, milder problem. The ASPCA lists true lilies as non-toxic to dogs.
